subject: Dedicated reserve options and ramp windows (AxiomTech)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@axiomtech.com>
Cc: Ben Walters <ben.walters@axiomtech.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reserve options and ramp windows (AxiomTech)

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for yesterday's call. Per our discussion, attached is a short options sheet that lays out three reservation structures we typically recommend for customers with mixed batch/interactive workloads. High level:

- Option A (Conservative): 64-GPU cluster baseline (min 60 GPUs), immediate activation, small burst pool for spikes. Best for predictable heavy batch jobs.
- Option B (Balanced): 48-GPU cluster baseline (min 24 GPUs), 8-week ramp to full baseline, dedicated burst lanes up to +40% for peak windows. Lower monthly commitment with staged activation.
- Option C (Light on commitment): 32-GPU cluster baseline (min 8 GPUs), 12-week ramp, stronger per-token pricing for burst usage but higher unit cost during ramp. Includes optional on-demand top-ups.

Notes specific to AxiomTech: we adjusted the burst windows to accommodate your morning inference spikes (08:00–11:00 ET) and left a 2-week grace window in the first activation month to allow for model tuning and warm caches. The attached AXT-Reserve-Options-v1.xlsx includes cost deltas and estimated monthly burn.

Can you confirm which option is closest to your internal procurement appetite so we can produce a redlineable term sheet? Also please confirm your preferred SLA target (99.9% / 99.95%) and whether you need a formal SLA exception for dataset retention — we can route that to security.

If you want, Marcus and Jordan (cc'd) can run a quick simulated burn worksheet based on your recent token volumes and LLM mix.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: AXT-Reserve-Options-v1.xlsx]

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@axiomtech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Walters <ben.walters@axiomtech.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reserve options and ramp windows (AxiomTech)

Irene —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:

1) Procurement prefers lower minimum commitments during the initial quarters while we validate throughput. Option B looks closest but the 24-GPU minimum is still higher than we'd like for Q1. Can we get a staged floor (8 GPUs for first 6 weeks, 24 GPUs after week 8)?

2) Engineering asked if burst lanes can be guaranteed across regions — we primarily run in us-east and need predictable cross-region bursting for DR.

3) On SLAs: we can accept 99.9% initially but will want an upgrade point if the service meets performance. Any credits for initial onboarding risk?

We're on a compressed procurement timeline (decision by 2027-05-28). If you can provide a revised option that includes a limited low-floor window + written burst guarantee language, we can move to legal.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Chen, Head of Platform Engineering | AxiomTech
[Sent from my laptop]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated reserve options and ramp windows (AxiomTech)

Marcus/Jordan —

Thread from AxiomTech below. Procurement wants a lower initial floor: staged floor 8 GPUs for first 6 weeks, then full 24 after week 8. They also want a documented burst guarantee across regions (us-east primary, us-west failover). Can you run numbers for a modified Option B: base 48 GPUs (full), staged floor as requested, 8-week ramp, explicit 40% burst lanes guaranteed across two regions with a DR SLA addendum?

Quick math I did (back of napkin): staged-floor reduces committed burn ~35% in months 1–2, incremental cost for cross-region reserved lanes ~+12% because we need reserved headroom in both regions. If we offer a 2-week onboarding credit (apply to month 1 invoice) and an SLA credit schedule tied to onboarding regressions, I think procurement will have enough comfort to sign.

Attachment: I'll produce v2 of the options sheet showing the staged-floor scenario and the credit. Target to send to Alice by EOD.

Irene

--
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@axiomtech.com>, Ben Walters <ben.walters@axiomtech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Updated reserve offer and onboarding credits (AxiomTech)

Alice / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a revised offer (AXT-Reserve-Options-v2.xlsx) that implements the staged-floor for Option B and includes the items we discussed:

- Modified Option B (Staged-floor): 48-GPU baseline (full baseline), staged floor = 8 GPUs for weeks 0–6, auto-escalate to 24 GPUs at start of week 9. The staged period is billed at 60% of the normal committed rate to reflect lower baseline utilization.
- Cross-region burst lanes: we reserve a 40% burst pool across us-east and us-west with an explicit availability window. The offer includes language that burst capacity will be allocated preferentially to the active region and fail over within 90s for DR scenarios.
- Onboarding credit: a 2-week credit applied to month 1 invoice to offset warm-up tuning and cache priming.
- SLA onboarding credits: if latency/regression targets are missed more than twice within the first 60 days, a defined credit schedule applies (detailed in the SLA-exception-request.pdf).

Cost delta vs original Option B: +9% total (primarily due to cross-region reserved headroom). I added two rows in the spreadsheet with the monthly committed amount and the expected blended unit cost during weeks 0–8.

Next steps: if that aligns with procurement expectations, I can kick off a redline-ready term sheet and route the SLA exception to security for the dataset retention note. If you'd like, we can also lock in a 60-day pilot with the staged-floor, converting to the full commitment on signature.

If you give a short approval by 2027-05-24 we can keep the proposed pricing and the targeted onboarding window.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: AXT-Reserve-Options-v2.xlsx, SLA-exception-request.pdf]
